setpieces.title: Special events
setpieces.intro: Seven turning points, reconstructed in 3D on the globe. Scale and time are compressed.

messines.title: The mines of Messines
messines.teaser: Nineteen mines erupt under the German line within seconds.

beats.text: For months, British, Canadian and Australian tunnellers dug beneath the German-held Messines Ridge.
Nineteen mines, packed with hundreds of tonnes of ammonal, wait under the German front line.
The mines are fired within about 20 seconds of each other.
The ridge is torn open by huge craters; the blast was reportedly heard as far away as London.
Behind a creeping barrage, British, Irish, Australian and New Zealand infantry take the ridge.

dunkirk.title: Dunkirk evacuation
dunkirk.teaser: The mole, the beach and the Channel: an army escapes by sea under fire.

beats.text: Trapped on the coast, British and French troops wait in long queues. Operation Dynamo begins.
The narrow breakwater becomes a lifeline. Destroyers and other large vessels take soldiers aboard directly from the mole.
Yachts, fishing boats and lifeboats reach the shallows, ferrying men from the beach to ships offshore.
Ju 87 dive-bombers attack the evacuation. Bombs throw up columns of seawater as the rescue continues.
Spitfires and Hurricanes help defend the evacuation, intercepting German aircraft over the coast and inland.
Loaded vessels head for England. Naval crews and small craft keep returning for more men.
Dynamo ends with 338,226 troops evacuated. French rear guards bought vital time; many men were still left behind.

pearl-harbor.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
pearl-harbor.teaser: Six Japanese carriers strike the US Pacific Fleet at anchor.

beats.text: Six Japanese aircraft carriers north of Oahu launch their aircraft.
About 350 aircraft, in two waves, fly south toward Oahu.
The attack begins. Torpedo bombers skim in low against Battleship Row.
Bombs strike the fleet; the forward magazine of USS Arizona explodes.
All eight battleships in the harbour are damaged, and four are sunk.
About 2,400 Americans are killed. The next day the United States declares war on Japan.

midway.title: Battle of Midway
midway.teaser: In minutes, US dive bombers turn the war in the Pacific.

beats.text: Four Japanese carriers steam northwest of Midway; Enterprise, Hornet and Yorktown wait to the northeast.
US torpedo bombers attack first, low over the water, and suffer heavy losses.
High above, SBD Dauntless dive bombers from Enterprise and Yorktown find the Japanese carriers.
Within minutes Akagi, Kaga and Soryu are hit and burning.
Aircraft from Hiryu cripple Yorktown; later that afternoon Hiryu is hit too.
All four Japanese fleet carriers are lost. Midway is widely seen as a turning point of the Pacific War.

d-day.title: D-Day, the Normandy landings
d-day.teaser: The largest seaborne invasion in history lands on five beaches.

beats.text: British gliders land beside the Caen canal bridge. Minutes later the 6th Airborne jumps east of the Orne.
About 13,000 men of the US 82nd and 101st Airborne jump over the Cotentin. Flak scatters them across fields and flooded marsh.
Some 6,900 vessels reach the five beaches. Transports anchor 18 km out and lower their landing craft.
Battleships, cruisers and destroyers open fire on the Atlantic Wall bunkers.
Hundreds of B-24s bomb through cloud. Afraid of hitting their own boats, they release late, and most bombs fall kilometres inland.
At Omaha the defences are intact: most amphibious tanks sink and the first wave is pinned on the sand. At Utah the landing meets little resistance.
The British land at Gold and Sword, with Free French commandos at Sword, and the Canadians at Juno. Tanks come ashore with the first waves.

About 156,000 Allied troops are ashore. At Omaha they hold only a thin strip, and the 21st Panzer counterattacks from Caen. Poles, Norwegians, Australians, New Zealanders, Dutch and others also took part.

hiroshima.title: Hiroshima
hiroshima.teaser: The first atomic bomb used in war.

beats.text: Morning over Hiroshima. Homes, streets and bridges fill the islands of the Ōta River delta.
The B-29 Enola Gay approaches with two accompanying aircraft. The distinctive Aioi Bridge is the aiming point.
Little Boy is released. The fall takes about 43 seconds; time is compressed in this reconstruction.
The bomb explodes in the air, about 600 metres above the city. A blinding flash precedes the blast.
A towering cloud rises above the delta. Dust and smoke obscure the streets below.
Heat, blast and fires devastate Hiroshima. Near the centre, the shell of the Industrial Promotion Hall remains standing.
Tens of thousands of people die, and many more suffer lasting injuries and illness. The surviving Dome becomes a memorial for peace.

nagasaki.title: Nagasaki
nagasaki.teaser: Three days later, a second atomic bomb.

beats.text: Nagasaki stretches between steep hills. Homes, factories, railway lines and Urakami Cathedral fill the valley.
Cloud and smoke obscure Kokura. The B-29 Bockscar turns to Nagasaki, where a break in the clouds permits the bombing run.
Fat Man is released over the Urakami Valley. Time is compressed in this reconstruction.
The bomb explodes about 500 metres above the valley. A brilliant flash is followed by the blast.
The cloud rises above the hills. Dust and smoke spread through Urakami, north of the city centre.
Homes, factories and the cathedral are devastated. The surrounding hills shape the destruction and partly shelter other districts.
Tens of thousands of people die. Survivors carry the consequences for the rest of their lives, and the city becomes a voice for peace.
